Validate indicator calculations against official DHS values

Source: R/validate.R
bdhs_validate.Rd

Computes national estimates with bdhs_estimate() and compares them with the official values published by the DHS Program API (bundled as bdhs_indicators). Use it to check that your copy of the data and the package's definitions reproduce the published figures before analysing subgroups or pooled rounds.

Usage

bdhs_validate(data, indicators = NULL, tolerance = 0.5, survey = NULL)

Arguments

data

A BDHS recode data frame for one round (or pooled rounds).

indicators

Indicator ids to validate. NULL (default) uses every indicator for the recode and round that has an official DHS value.

tolerance

Allowed absolute difference, in the units of the official value (percentage points for percentages).

survey

Optional survey reference, overriding detection.

Value

A tibble with columns survey_id, indicator, label, api_id, computed, official, diff (computed - official), tolerance (effective tolerance), pass, n_unweighted and official_n_unweighted (the official unweighted denominator, when published).

Details

The official value is the national total (is_total) for the round, taken for the indicator's reference period (by_variable_label, e.g. "Three years preceding the survey") when the indicator defines one, and the DHS-preferred value (is_preferred) otherwise. Indicators defined as a sum of API categories (for example postnatal care within two days) are compared with the sum.

A computation passes when abs(computed - official) does not exceed tolerance (scaled for indicators in other units, e.g. 0.1 x tolerance for the total fertility rate) plus half a unit of the official value's rounding precision.

Examples

# Simulated data are random, so they are not expected to pass:
kr <- bdhs_simulate(2017, "KR")
bdhs_validate(kr, c("rh_del_facility", "rh_del_csection"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   survey_id indicator       label api_id computed official  diff tolerance pass 
#>   <chr>     <chr>           <chr> <chr>     <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1 BD2017DHS rh_del_facility Deli… RH_DE…     54.7     49.4  5.34      0.55 FALSE
#> 2 BD2017DHS rh_del_csection Deli… RH_DE…     33.7     32.7  1.03      0.55 FALSE
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_unweighted <int>, official_n_unweighted <dbl>
